clue.text: An Italian bacon pate can't possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of pate and can't may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone insists an Italian bacon pâté simply cannot be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges PATE and CANT (the apostrophe adds no letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Pancetta is a cured pork belly from Italy, a kind of bacon.

clue.text: Ring gossip about note

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Ring gossip about note' (5) for ARENA: no word for gossip goes round a note to give ARENA (AREA round N would need 'area'); likely an OCR or source error.

clue.text: Intellectual's smart footwear

parts.note: smart means clever
clogs are wooden-soled footwear

explanation.surface: A brainy person shows off a fashionable pair of shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all, someone showily brainy, is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Metalworker can, with German, in silence

parts.note: a can is a tin

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the call for silence

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A craftsman works quietly alongside a German colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'can' as a verb; it is a noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith is a craftsman making things from tinplate, so a metalworker.

clue.text: What bird flu can make you?

definitions.text: What bird flu can make you?

parts.words: What bird flu can make you?
parts.note: read literally, an illness caught from birds would leave you as unwell as a talking pet bird; the British idiom actually means bitterly disappointed

explanation.surface: A question about the effects of avian influenza.
explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase, much used by footballers, means utterly fed up; the clue takes it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes deep disappointment, playfully read here as illness caught from a bird.

clue.text: Trading in sacred things in man's yard

parts.note: Simon is a man's name

explanation.surface: Religious relics are being sold in someone's back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: The word comes from Simon Magus, who tried to buy spiritual power, so the name is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Simony is the buying or selling of church offices or holy privileges.

clue.text: Resting in stable

explanation.definitionFit: Static describes something motionless and something unchanging or steady.

clue.text: Bushy-tailed creature, cunning, trapped by servants

indicators.note: trapped by puts the word for cunning inside the word for servants

parts.note: servants are men, as in a lord's men
cunning, as in craft or guile, means art

explanation.surface: A sly animal with a fluffy tail is caught by the household staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The marten is a weasel-like mammal with a long bushy tail.

clue.text: Active at night? No? Go in around end of April

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the word for go inside the abbreviation for around

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around
a go is a turn

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of April

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you're active at night and urges you to come in at the end of April.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go in around' reads like an instruction to enter; the question mark flags that the definition describes owls and bats rather than any one sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nocturnal animals are awake and busy after dark.

clue.text: Small number crossing river, British one

indicators.note: crossing puts the river abbreviation across, inside, the number

parts.note: seven is a small number

explanation.surface: A few people wade across a British waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' looks like the definition; it supplies R, and 'British one' means a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is the longest waterway in Britain, flowing through Wales and England.

clue.text: Not a real diamond, but it's revered by Patrick

parts.note: something not real is a sham
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A fake gem is still held dear by a man called Patrick.
explanation.walkthrough: Patrick is Saint Patrick, Ireland's patron saint, said to have used the three-leafed plant to explain the Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: The trefoil plant is Ireland's emblem, linked by legend to its patron saint.

clue.text: Pub close to picturesque mere

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: close to picks the final letter of picturesque

explanation.surface: A tavern stands near a pretty lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like a lake; it means nothing more than, as in a bare minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean nothing more than, as in the bare minimum and a mere pittance.

clue.text: Mother and child, say, protected by one sister with weapon

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Mother and child, say, protected by one sister with weapon' (7,3) for MACHINEGUN: no parse of these words gives MACHINE; likely an OCR or misattached clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Mother and child, say, protected by one sister with weapon

clue.text: Venus usually gave tennis-playing ultimate in endeavour

indicators.note: playing signals the letters of gave and tennis are put into play in a new order
ultimate in picks the final letter of endeavour

explanation.surface: Venus Williams typically gave her all on the tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the tennis player; 'playing' rearranges GAVE TENNIS, and R ends endeavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus is the bright planet most often seen in the west after sunset.

clue.text: Port may be diluted in Malta, note, for money

indicators.note: in places the word for diluted inside the altered island name
for means the note takes the place of the money abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
c is a musical note
cut means diluted, as of a drug

explanation.surface: Port wine might be watered down on Malta, with a note left to pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' is the Indian city, not the wine; MALTA with C for M gives CALTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Now Kolkata, the city is a major seaport on the Hooghly river in India.

clue.text: Place for mooring in port

definitions.meaning: a spot where a ship lies at anchor
the city in Alaska, a seaport

explanation.definitionFit: Both a berth where vessels anchor and the Alaskan seaport city share this name.

clue.text: For this mount you should get stake back!

indicators.note: back means the word for stake is read from the end

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a mountain is told to expect a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' sounds like getting your money back; it turns ANTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily.

clue.text: Poor colt unlikely to produce good form

indicators.note: unlikely, in the sense of improbable, signals that poor and colt end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A weak young horse is not expected to show good racing form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'unlikely' rearranges POOR COLT.
explanation.definitionFit: Protocol is the code of correct conduct, so proper etiquette.

clue.text: Italian novelist taking in hard copy

indicators.note: taking in puts the hard abbreviation inside the novelist's name

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An Italian author gets a printout of his manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard copy' looks like one phrase; 'hard' gives H and 'copy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo repeats a sound, so it is an imitation or repeat.

clue.text: Gun lay next to sack

parts.note: a lay is a song or air
to sack is to plunder or rifle

explanation.surface: A weapon lies next to a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay' and 'sack' read as verb and noun; they are a song and a verb, plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: An air rifle is a firearm firing pellets by compressed air.

clue.text: Handsome young man getting Oscar after a ballot

indicators.note: after puts the Oscar letter behind the article and the vote

parts.note: a poll is a ballot
Oscar is O in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A good-looking youth wins an Oscar following a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: An Apollo is a handsome youth, after the Greek god.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek god of beauty, the name is used for any good-looking youth.

clue.text: Fern, perhaps, in salon, up the duff

indicators.note: duff, British slang for faulty or useless, signals that salon, up and the are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman sits in a hair salon, perhaps called Fern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the duff' is British slang for pregnant; 'Fern' looks like a name, but a fern is an example of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is often grown indoors as a potted greenery.

clue.text: Cut good wood

parts.note: ash is a wood

explanation.surface: A fine piece of timber is sawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A gash is a deep wound or slash.

clue.text: Steer clear of rear of juggernaut, or crash

parts.note: to steer clear of is to shun

indicators.note: rear of picks the final letter of juggernaut

explanation.surface: A driver avoids the back of a lorry to avoid a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: A juggernaut is a British word for a huge lorry. A shunt is British slang for a minor crash.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a shunt is a car collision, especially a rear-end one.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader with treaty prepared annexing Luxembourg

indicators.note: annexing means the reworked treaty takes in the Luxembourg letter
prepared means the letters of treaty are dressed into a new form

parts.note: L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A rebel chief draws up a pact by which Luxembourg is annexed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' turns TREATY into ATTYER, and 'annexing' places L inside it. Wat Tyler led England's Peasants' Revolt of 1381.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the English Peasants' Revolt against Richard II in 1381.

clue.text: See 7
Stop working in block

definitions.meaning: of a machine, to shut off
a figure cut from card, or a stencil block

explanation.definitionFit: An engine can cut out, and a cutout is a shape cut out of card or a block.

clue.text: Slowly locking a shed

indicators.note: locking means the musical direction closes round the letter

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for slowly

explanation.surface: Someone slowly padlocks a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: LENTO is a tempo marking in music.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple outbuilding propped against a wall.

clue.text: Suffer later, with toe being broken

indicators.note: being broken means the letters of later and toe are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone will feel the pain afterwards, having broken a toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer' means put up with, not feel pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer fools is to put up with them, so bear or endure.
